rule: Encounter = trigger + fixed roster + lifetime. Trigger is a radius step-in or a boundary crossing with a cooldown window. Roster is a fixed composition around one prop (roamers leashed to a home point, one bound NPC). Lifetime is a fixed clock from creation (field camps), a clock restarted on each entry (base camps), or a progress meter that resets on a timer (lair). Escort is a follow order with a check timer, arrival pay, a grace before abandon, and a per-player cooldown. Defects: camp decay ignores occupancy (D1); proximity spawner fires one spawn per trigger and ignores its count (D2); ML escort death leaves the master bound (D3).
keep: fixed roster around one prop as the camp identity
boundary-crossing trigger with a visible grace clock
bound NPC who calls out on approach
lair meter that fills in fifths and levels up with a sound and a light
escort follow with arrival pay, grace before abandon, per-player cooldown
two lifetimes: fixed clock for field camps, restart-on-entry for base camps
change: decay re-arms while a player is inside (D1)
proximity trigger fills to count, not one at a time (D2)
escort release runs on player death (D3)
roster capped at three active in engagement (MAX_ATTACKERS)
our own names and palette; no donor strings
pack-wave respawn, if used, gated by a per-tick NPC budget
look_test: On a 375-wide phone in one zone: (1) a camp with three roamers within six tiles, a bound NPC two tiles off centre who calls out on approach, and a visible five-minute ring; judge readability and whether the ring reads as leaving. (2) An ambush ring of twelve tiles spawning one aggressive enemy beside the player; judge surprise vs spawn pop, then add a half-second warning flash and judge again. (3) A lair altar with a five-part meter and a sound and light at full; judge the level-up beat.
